clue.text: Depressed by loss of feathers

parts.note: down is the soft fine feathering of a bird
feathers cast are shed or thrown off, so a loss is a casting

explanation.surface: A moulting bird looks thoroughly fed up after losing its plumage.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'loss of feathers' as feathers cast off: DOWN, then CAST. 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone downcast is low in spirits, a synonym for dejected.

clue.text: Note the world shortage

parts.note: D is a musical note in the scale
our planet, the globe we live on

explanation.surface: A remark that the whole planet is running short of something.
explanation.definitionFit: A dearth is a scarcity or lack of something.

clue.text: I hunt down suspect in murder mystery

indicators.note: suspect read as a verb-like adjective meaning dubious or unsound, so the letters are not to be trusted in their order

explanation.surface: A detective tracks down a suspect in a crime novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suspect' rearranges the nine letters of I HUNT DOWN; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A whodunnit is a detective story where the reader guesses the killer.

clue.text: Cold store base

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
a heap is a pile or stockpile, a store of things

explanation.surface: A refrigerated warehouse at a military base.
explanation.definitionFit: Base in the sense of low and vulgar, meaning shoddy or of little worth.

clue.text: How a sailor makes ends meet?

definitions.text: How a sailor makes ends meet?

parts.words: How a sailor makes ends meet?
parts.note: the idiom about scraping a living is read literally: a sailor joins rope ends by interweaving their strands

explanation.definitionFit: Sailors join two ropes by interweaving the strands, a technique named for that joining.

clue.text: Literary type inclined to impress

parts.note: not a bookish person but a printed typeface that slopes, used for emphasis

explanation.definitionFit: Italic print is a sloping typeface used to emphasise words in text.

clue.text: A chart showing current changes

parts.note: current suggests the latest news, but here it is the flow of the sea rising and falling

explanation.definitionFit: A table listing the times of high and low water at a place.

clue.text: He doesn't win new roles

indicators.note: new letters are made from old ones, so the word roles is rearranged

explanation.surface: An actor who misses out on fresh parts.
explanation.definitionFit: A loser is someone defeated in a contest.

clue.text: Name in credit as thriller-writer

indicators.note: the name word sits inside the credit abbreviation

parts.note: CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit
a handle is slang for a name or nickname

explanation.surface: A novelist's name appears in the film credits.
explanation.walkthrough: Raymond Chandler wrote hard-boiled detective thrillers featuring Philip Marlowe.
explanation.definitionFit: Raymond Chandler was an American crime novelist, creator of the private eye Marlowe.

clue.text: A lovable disposition may be most important

indicators.note: a disposition is an arrangement, so these letters are set out afresh

explanation.surface: A sweet nature is perhaps the thing that matters most.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disposition' looks like character, but it means arrangement: rearrange A LOVABLE. 'may be' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Above all is an idiom meaning more than anything else, chiefly.

clue.text: From this port seas do appear rough

indicators.note: rough water is churned up, so the letters of seas do are tossed into a new order

explanation.surface: Leaving harbour, the sailors see choppy water ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rough' rearranges SEAS DO; 'From' and 'appear' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Odessa is a major Black Sea harbour city in Ukraine.

clue.text: Arranged a takeover, having inside information

indicators.note: the phrase has the letters sitting within it, spanning the words

explanation.surface: A company buyout organised with the help of insider knowledge.
explanation.definitionFit: Data are facts and figures, the raw material of knowledge.

clue.text: Hit the first bump

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word the is taken

parts.note: a hump is a raised bump or mound

explanation.surface: Striking the opening bump on a road.
explanation.definitionFit: To thump is to strike heavily, a synonym for hit.

clue.text: Three-card trick has been given a licence

indicators.note: a trick deceives, so the letters of three-card are juggled

explanation.surface: A card sharp running the three-card trick has been granted a permit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trick' rearranges THREE CARD; the three-card trick is a street con. 'has been' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A chartered body or professional holds a formal licence or charter.

clue.text: Tries to catch "Points of View"

definitions.meaning: goes fishing with rod and line, trying to land a fish
perspectives or slants on a story

explanation.surface: Someone tries to get on a well-known TV viewers' feedback programme.
explanation.walkthrough: Points of View is a long-running BBC programme airing viewers' letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Fishing with a line, and approaches or standpoints from which something is seen.

clue.text: An expert swimmer in the cavalry

definitions.meaning: a beach or pool rescuer must swim strongly
a member of the ..., a British household cavalry regiment

explanation.definitionFit: A beach rescuer, and a trooper of the British household cavalry regiment.

clue.text: A doctor stood up for him

definitions.note: the definition is a pronoun standing for a man's name

parts.note: MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's qualification
rose means got to one's feet

explanation.surface: A doctor took the stand on behalf of a patient.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is just 'him': the clue builds a man's name. 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambrose is a male first name, so the pronoun stands for such a man.

clue.text: Band of gold put on box by artist

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece placed on top of the next

parts.note: OR is gold in heraldry
a chest is a large box
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A gold ornament placed on a box by a painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put on' places OR above CHEST in the down light; 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchestra is a band of musicians.

clue.text: The favourite comes round and takes part in the event

indicators.note: the word comes goes round the other piece, enclosing it

parts.note: a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet

explanation.surface: The race favourite comes back round and enters the contest.
explanation.definitionFit: To compete is to take part in a contest.

clue.text: Love to appear in costume but has no chance

indicators.note: the letter turns up within the costume word

parts.note: an outfit is a set of clothes
O is love, a zero score in tennis

explanation.surface: An actor loves to be in fancy dress yet has no hope of a part.
explanation.walkthrough: Out of it is an idiom for having no chance of winning. 'to' and 'but' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Out of it means eliminated from contention, unable to win.

clue.text: Old city conservative showing a change of heart?

indicators.note: the central letters of the word swap places, a change at its heart

parts.note: a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A Tory politician who has switched sides.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle letters of TORY trade places: the O moves after the R.
explanation.definitionFit: Troy is the ancient city besieged by the Greeks in Homer's Iliad.

clue.text: What one may do to one's teeth if you bend a nail?

definitions.text: What one may do to one's teeth
definitions.meaning: grit or clamp the jaw tight
hammering over the protruding point of a nail to fix it

explanation.definitionFit: To grit the jaw tight, and to fasten a driven nail by bending its point over.

clue.text: Shakespearean play house

parts.note: not a theatre such as the Globe but a family house in one of the plays, Juliet's

explanation.definitionFit: Juliet's family in Romeo and Juliet are a noble house of Verona.

clue.text: Head of English allowed to evoke response

indicators.note: the first letter of the word English is taken

parts.note: licit means lawful, permitted

explanation.surface: An English department chief permitted to provoke a reaction.
explanation.definitionFit: To elicit is to draw out a reply or reaction.

clue.text: Drama circle for preschool kids

definitions.note: the definition describes what the gathering is for rather than naming it

parts.note: a play is a drama
a circle of people is a group

explanation.surface: A theatre club for young children.
explanation.definitionFit: A playgroup is an informal nursery session where under-fives play together.

clue.text: Unusually eager to come to terms

indicators.note: in an unusual way, so the letters of eager appear in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone surprisingly keen to strike a deal.
explanation.definitionFit: To agree is to reach accord, settling on terms.

clue.text: A fisherman will use many a spinner

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, many
a reel spins to wind in the line

explanation.surface: An angler will need plenty of spinning lures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spinner' suggests a fishing lure, but it is the turning reel.
explanation.definitionFit: A creel is a wicker basket an angler carries the catch in.

clue.text: Animal arrived, then left

parts.note: came is the past tense of come

explanation.surface: Something turned up and then departed.
explanation.definitionFit: A camel is a humped desert beast.

clue.text: The first city getting capital investment

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word The is taken

parts.note: urban means of a city

explanation.surface: The leading city receives money for development.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital investment' sounds financial, but capital is the head and investment clothing. 'getting' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Capital means head and investment means clothing, so headwear wrapped round the head.

clue.text: A number claim it is changeable, like the weather

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

indicators.note: liable to change, so the letters of claim it shift about

explanation.surface: Some say the weather is variable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changeable' rearranges CLAIM IT into LIMATIC, after C. 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Climatic means relating to long-term weather patterns.

clue.text: Firm rearranged dates before the end of May

indicators.note: the letters of dates are put in a different order
the final letter of the word May

explanation.surface: A company moved its schedule ahead of late May.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm' looks like a company, matching the business-diary surface, but it is the adjective. 'rearranged' and 'the end of' are the indicators; 'before' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Firm in the sense of stable and secure, not wobbling.

clue.text: Resolute man set out to catch law-breaker

indicators.note: the start word holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: to start is to set out on a journey

indicators.note: breaking the word law scrambles its letters

explanation.surface: A determined man went off to arrest a criminal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'law-breaker' reads as criminal, but 'breaker' scrambles the word in front of it to LWA, and 'to catch' holds that inside the synonym for set out.
explanation.definitionFit: A stalwart is a staunch, dependable supporter.
